title: Detection of potential adverse orofacial side effects in patients with obstructive sleep apnoea and hypoglossal nerve stimulation therapy
summary: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a common sleep disorder that results in increased breathing resistance, interruption of respiratory flow, increased oxygen desaturation, and subsequent awakening reactions due to upper airway weakness. A potential treatment for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) involves nocturnal stimulation of the tongue. The objective of the planned study is to identify potential side effects on teeth and bite caused by nocturnal tongue pressure.

interventions.name: Patients with obstructive sleep apnea undergoing hypoglossal nerve stimulation therapy are recruited and examined to evaluate potential undesired orofacial side effects. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Presence of anterior teeth in the upper and lower jaws
• Signed informed consent form available
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of informed consent to participate in the study
• Combination therapy with CPAP or mandibular advancement device
• Absence of incisors in the upper and lower jaw
• Generalized severe periodontitis
• Nighttime use of a bite splint
• Fixed retainer in the upper and lower jaw
